description.from:
Change how Kanbus abbreviates an issue's hash prefix for display (CLI and console). Short IDs currently show 6 characters (for example kbs-60bf38).

New design: a dynamic prefix length.
- By default, show 4 characters of the hash in short IDs (for example kbs-60bf).
- Detect collisions in context. When rendering a set of issues (for example the output of kbs list), if two or more issues in that set share the same first 4 characters, widen the displayed prefix for that list or session only. Add characters as needed until every displayed ID in that context is unique.
- The full original ID is always kept. This changes only how much of the ID is shown in a given context, never the stored ID.
- Unique-prefix lookups (kbs show <prefix>, --parent <prefix>, and so on) keep working, and existing longer references in comments, commits and docs still resolve.

Why:
- 4 characters saves tokens for agents and cuts visual noise for people reading the UI.
- Collisions at 4 characters are rare.
- When a collision does happen, the extra characters are paid only in the context where it occurs, not across every ID everywhere.

Out of scope: GitHub's commit-hash display.
description.to:
Change how Kanbus abbreviates an issue's hash prefix for display (CLI and console). Short IDs currently show 6 characters (for example kbs-60bf38).

New design: a dynamic prefix length.
- By default, show 4 characters of the hash in short IDs (for example kbs-60bf). The default is configurable via `short_id_length` in .kanbus.yml; Beads compatibility mode implies 6 unless explicitly set.
- Collision checks are project-wide, not just within the visible list: a displayed short ID is unique among the live issues sharing its project key (shared + local together). Within a rendered set, only colliding groups widen, iteratively, with no cap on width.
- The full original ID is always kept. This changes only how much of the ID is shown in a given context, never the stored ID.
- Unique-prefix lookups (kbs show <prefix>, --parent <prefix>, and so on) keep working via hyphen-insensitive matching, and existing longer references in comments, commits and docs still resolve. When a prefix matches multiple issues, the disambiguation picker (task kbs-26d651) presents the candidates; non-interactive callers get a structured error with full IDs and a stable exit code, and retry once with a full ID.
- Stored text (wiki pages, story-directory paths, commit messages, summaries, agent provenance commands, newly written references) uses full IDs; display-only contexts use the formatter. `kbs validate` flags stored references that have become ambiguous.

Why:
- 4 characters saves tokens for agents and cuts visual noise for people reading the UI.
- Collisions at 4 characters are uncommon per pair but expected at board scale; the extra characters are paid only where they occur, and the picker makes the rare ambiguity recoverable instead of fatal.
- Full IDs in stored text keep long-lived references stable.

Out of scope: GitHub's commit-hash display.
